stories.title: 50 leaders in Dublin for State's largest diplomatic event
stories.summary: The largest diplomatic undertaking in Irish history gets under way this morning as Taoiseach Micheál Martin hosts the ninth European Political Community summit at the Convention Centre Dublin. The event is the logistical high point of Ireland's EU presidency and will be characterised by a massive security operation and traffic lockdown as the State prepares to welcome as many as 50 heads of state and government, as well as leaders of EU institutions. While there has been no conclusive evidence thus far, there are suspicions that the threats are part of Russia’s ongoing hybrid warfare efforts against European countries supporting Ukraine. In September 2025, ahead of the last EPC meeting hosted by an EU member state, Copenhagen airport and a number of Danish military bases were subject to a range of unexplained drone attacks. The EPC brings together over 50 EU and non-EU leaders arriving from all corners of the continent, from Iceland to Armenia. Canadian prime minister Mark Carney will join the summit, as will NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

stories.title: UK economy sees biggest expansion in over 2 years in Q3
stories.summary: The UK economy grew at the fastest rate in two and a half years in the third quarter of 2026, helped by a boost from artificial intelligence and extending a strong first-half, official figures showed today. Gross domestic product expanded by 0.7% in the three months from July to September. This was in line with a Reuters poll of economists, but faster than its 0.5% growth in the second quarter of the year and the strongest calendar-quarter growth since the first quarter of 2024, the Office for National Statistics said. On a rolling three-month basis, the growth was the fastest since May. The annual growth rate picked up to 1.9% in the third quarter, the strongest reading since the fourth quarter in 2024, and also in line with the 1.9% median forecast in the Reuters poll. The services sector, which makes up the majority of the UK economy, grew 0.9% on the quarter and a stronger than expected 0.2% in September alone.

stories.title: Lessons loaded as O'Shea & Ireland make beeline for Linz
stories.summary: As Dara O'Shea makes his way to Linz alongside his team-mates this afternoon, the load that the Republic of Ireland defender will have to bear will be slightly lighter than what he had to shoulder during the last UEFA Nations League window. The Boys in Green were in the eye of the storm as late September morphed into early October amid the furore over the controversial fixtures against Israel. In the temporary absence of captain Nathan Collins and the peerless leadership of veteran Séamus Coleman, it was O'Shea who assumed the captaincy. That mantle also brought the responsibility of speaking to the media on behalf of the players in the build-up to opening group game in Kosovo. That appearance was one of the last times any of the players were heard from during that extended four-game window. It also came just three days before the fractious events of Debrecen when players conducted a vote at the team hotel about whether they would fulfil the first Israel match, whilst goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu had signalled his resolve to sit out the fixtures.

stories.title: Celebrating the new wave of Irish hip-hop
stories.summary: I am convinced that Ireland has one of the best music scenes in the world, writes Darragh MacManus. The amount of talent in Irish rap specifically is astonishing for a country of this size. I have been attending gigs all over and listening extensively to what our nation has to offer. Here are three artists who I believe are the new wave of Irish hip-hop: I first saw deathtoricky live at Pawn Shop in May 2025. With only four singles released on Spotify at the time, he performed a set that was short and sweet. This epitomises Ricky's sound: here for a good time, not a long time. Most of his songs are under two minutes, so I find myself listening to his music on repeat. It is addictive, explosive and most of all, fun. I always have a smile on my face listening to deathtoricky. His latest EP, pre life, is no exception. It begins with ‘lemon haze’, a self-produced track layered with ethereal synths and peppered with producer tags. This song develops into a stuttered jerk-style beat with braggadocious claims of doing donuts in a Honda Accord. Other highlights include ‘crystal clear’, which has glittery guitar loops mixed with hazy hypnotic flows and ‘falling out’ which has pulsing synths paired with Auto-Tune falsetto vocals. deathtoricky is experimental but authentic. You can really feel he had a good time making this music. The collaboration I didn't know I needed in my life. This link-up feels like the two biggest messers in class working on a school project together. Enniscorthy’s own Lil Skag has been dropping strong singles since 2023. The 'D12 drifter’, Sugabooo, released his first official song last year, but early tracks were forwarded through WhatsApp. In his own words, ‘I used to get catfished on Viber / I used to put tunes out on WhatsApp’.

stories.title: Garth Brooks tickets go on sale for 10 Irish shows
stories.summary:
Tickets for Garth Brooks' 10 Irish concerts go on sale at 8am this morning, with the country music superstar set to perform in five cities next summer. The US singer will play two shows each in Belfast, Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick and Cork during May and June 2027, with no Dublin dates scheduled. Tickets are available through Ticketmaster, with standing tickets for the Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick and Cork concerts priced at €136.25 and seated tickets costing €156.25, before additional service charges. Read more:
Garth Brooks: 'A hundred gigs in Ireland wouldn't be enough' The tour opens at Boucher Road Playing Fields in Belfast on Friday 21 and Saturday 22 May, before moving to Pearse Stadium in Galway on Saturday 29 and Sunday 30 May. Brooks will then perform at UPMC Nowlan Park in Kilkenny on Friday 4 and Saturday 5 June, followed by TUS Gaelic Grounds in Limerick on Friday 11 and Saturday 12 June.

stories.title: Celebrating Día de los Muertos in San Antonio, Texas
stories.summary: Walking amid giant skeletons and elegant Catrinas in classic black, deep red and purple dresses, lace ruffles, colourful headbands and elaborate wide-brimmed hats, you could be mistaken for thinking it's the Day of the Dead in Mexico City. But I'm in its neighbour, San Antonio in Texas, 150 miles from the Mexican border, which stages the biggest Día de los Muertos festival in the US every autumn. In fact, it's thanks to the opening scene of the 2015 James Bond movie Spectre – where 007 weaves his way through a fictional Day of the Dead parade in Mexico City – that the event has become such a huge extravaganza. The following year, the tourist board ensured fiction was turned into reality, staging carnival processions and colourful floats, and in 2017, San Antonio, which has a 64% Hispanic population, with people of Mexican descent making up the majority, did its own version. It has grown, and the three-day Day of the Dead festival in San Antonio (the second largest city in the state behind Houston) is now the biggest in the US. It attracts thousands to its dazzling River Parade, a night-time procession of elaborately decorated barges, where performers dance, sing and play instruments to entertain the crowd.

stories.title: Two dead after apartment building in New York collapses
stories.summary: At least two people were killed and several others were injured after a three-story building next to a construction site collapsed in Brooklyn, in New York. The four-unit apartment building dating from 1930 collapsed and tumbled into the adjoining construction site where excavation work was under way and the cause was under investigation, said John Esposito, the city's fire department chief. The number of people who were at home when the building in the Flatbush area of Brooklyn collapsed at about 4pm (9pm Irish time) was not immediately known, officials said. They did not say how many workers were on the construction site at the time of the collapse. A firefighting crew that happened to be in the neighbourhood was on the scene within a minute of the collapse and helped pull the first victims from the debris, authorities told reporters at press conference last night. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at least two people were killed, and that more than 10 others were taken to local hospitals with a combination of critical and non-life-threatening injuries. City Fire Department Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said the overall number of known victims stood at 19 people, seven of them children. She declined to say whether the two dead were children or adults. A firefighter also suffered minor injuries, she said.

stories.title: Poundland owner urged to back protection extension
stories.summary: Gordon Brothers, the US investment firm that owns Poundland, must allow the discount retailer to have full access to its own bank accounts to give it a chance of securing a rescue deal, a senior British politician has said. Poundland filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators on October 29, giving the business 10 working days to find a rescue deal. The notice expired yesterday, but can be extended. The decision over an extension rests with Poundland's board, AlixPartners as administrators in waiting, the Financial Conduct Authority and the court. Representatives of Gordon Brothers appeared before parliament's Business and Trade Committee in private session yesterday. The committee is chaired by Labour politician Liam Byrne. "This is a moment of urgency, we hope that Poundland will basically extend the protection period that they enjoy quickly tonight so that we maximise the chance of getting a deal done that saves the business for the future," Byrne told Sky News after the session. "But to get that deal done Gordon Brothers need to make sure that there is full and fulsome access for Poundland to its own bank accounts."

stories.title: Gibson-Park raring to go after disrupted start to season
stories.summary: After a groin injury delayed his start to the season, Jamison Gibson-Park is excited to be "back in the mix" as he looks to kickstart his campaign. The Leinster and Ireland scrum-half came off the bench for the final 25 minutes of last Friday's 42-12 win against Argentina, for what was just his second appearance of the season. Having sat out Leinster's first four games of the campaign, the 34-year-old eventually returned for the province in their 24-18 win against Munster last month, getting 80 minutes under his belt ahead of joining Ireland's Nations Championship camp. However, with such limited gametime behind him, Ireland's first-choice scrum-half had to play second-fiddle to Craig Casey at Aviva Stadium last Friday, with the Munster man linking up impressively with Sam Prendergast as Ireland's attack hummed. With potentially one eye on next week's meeting with South Africa, Gibson-Park could come back into the starting team for Ireland on Saturday night when they host Fiji. And after Casey set a high standard last week, Gibson-Park is using that competition to drive him.

stories.title: How U2 put Windmill Lane Studios on the map
stories.summary: We present an extract from Windmill Lane Recording Studios: The Stories, The Sessions, The Sound, the new book by Tony Clayton-Lea and Mark Cunningham. stories.title: Éanna Hardwicke to be honoured as Cork festival opens
stories.summary: Cork actor Éanna Hardwicke will receive a special award tonight as the 71st Cork International Film Festival gets under way, with more than 200 films screening over the next 11 days. The Normal People and Saipan star will be presented with the Honorary Puttnam Award for his contribution to Irish cinema at the festival's opening gala at MTU Cork School of Music. Hardwicke will also take part in a public conversation about his career at the Arc Cinema on Friday. The festival opens with the Irish premiere of Lucy Lost, an animated film directed by Olivier Clert and based on Michael Morpurgo’s novel Listen to the Moon. The screening will feature a musical presentation and a Q&A with the director and composer Anne-Sophie Versnaeyen. Irish cinema features prominently in this year’s programme, including Ancestors, starring Hardwicke alongside Rupert Everett and Christina Hendricks.

stories.title: The 15 best Irish food books of 2026
stories.summary: Patrick Hanlon and Russell Alford are freelance food and travel writers who write at gastrogays.com and can be found on social media as @gastrogays If the landscape of food book publishing in Ireland in 2026 could be distilled into a few key words, it would be: eclectic, fast, flavourful. This year's crop of cookbooks and other food-focused books prioritise flavour over faff, efficiency over elaborate technique, and personality at every turn. From books about whiskey, cheese toasties and black pudding to one-pot winners and loaf-tin bakes, there’s a book for everyone in this selection. Here are 15 of this year’s best. "If there’s one thing I’ve learned cooking in restaurants, on television, and at home for the people I love, it’s this: great food doesn’t need to take all day," Mark Moriarty writes in the introduction of this third cookbook. In this tome, the top Irish chef is zoning in on speed and efficiency with comforting, reliable recipes, which he says are "the things I cook for myself, for my family, for friends who show up unannounced". Mark’s skill throughout his TV chef career (Off Duty Chef; Beyond The Menu; Cook Like a Chef) and accompanying cookbooks (Flavour; Season) has always been in empowering the home cook with chef-y know-how and making great cooking feel within reach, whatever the kitchen ability.

stories.title: Govt accused of trying to get 'defence on the cheap'
stories.summary: The Government is being called on to end the exclusion of senior Defence Force officers from allowances for overtime work, or to end the practice of rostering them for duties attracting such allowances. The Representative Association of Commissioned Officers (RACO) has made the call as the Defence Forces are deployed on Operation Fianna, the security operation for the European Political Community and European Council meetings taking place in Dublin today and tomorrow. It is the largest security operation in the history of the State. RACO said that senior officers, from the rank of Commandant/Naval Lieutenant Commander and above, are commanding the Joint Task Force and its land, maritime and air components. "They are directing counter-drone and air defence operations, leading maritime and air patrols, overseeing EOD and specialist operations, and coordinating with An Garda Síochána, Government departments and international partners," according to RACO. "They do this alongside, and often in command of, junior officers and enlisted personnel who receive security duty allowances at the rate of €68 per day before tax for the same operation.

stories.title: Nvidia board meets to decide CEO Huang's future
stories.summary: Nvidia's board was meeting late last night to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, as the world's dominant supplier of AI chips grapples with fallout from reports of two extramarital affairs involving its longtime leader. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the board meeting. The meeting marks a sharp shift from Sunday, when Nvidia's board expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team. Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of directors. Nvidia has 11 directors and considers all but Huang independent. Nvidia's stock slid more than 8% in extended trading after the Wall Street Journal first reported that the company was preparing to fire Huang. If those losses hold, Nvidia will have lost about $600 billion in market value since the board announced its investigation into his relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang alleged to be a Chinese spy.

stories.title: Coleman quality endures as 'decision time' looms - O'Shea
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland assistant John O'Shea says Séamus Coleman is aware that "decision time is coming" over his future and emphasised that the veteran defender's "quality" remains undiminished. Former Everton captain Coleman is with the Ireland squad in a hybrid role that encompasses training and a support role with the coaches ahead of the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Austria and Kosovo. At last Thursday's squad announcement, manager Heimir Hallgrimsson said the role had been envisaged with helping to tempt the 38-year-old to extend his playing career. On the eve of the Irish squad's departure to Linz for the Austria away match, O'Shea outlined the impact that Coleman has been having in his hybrid remit. "It's like what the boss said about it. It's us helping Seámus and Seámus is helping us really," he said as he spoke alongside defender Dara O'Shea at Wednesday's press conference at FAI HQ. "To see the impact he is having and the quality that remains in his ability and the driving and pushing he is doing for the group, it has been good to see him and not much has changed really."

stories.title: Democrat seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
stories.summary: Democrat Scott Colom has won his US Senate race in traditionally conservative Mississippi, networks have projected, making him the first African-American elected to the chamber from the southern state in more than 140 years. Mr Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, prevailed over Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in perhaps the most extraordinary seat flip of an already extraordinary US midterm election, in which Democrats crushed the Republicans to reclaim the majority in both chambers of Congress. Mr Colom's win adds sting to the stunning rebuke of President Donald Trump as voters around the country shunned his Republican Party, even in states that had not sent a Democrat to Washington in decades. The latest win, called yesterday by US news outlets that included CNN, NBC and CBS, will give Democrats 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with 44 for Republicans and one race - in the state of Alaska - still outstanding. Ms Hyde-Smith, in office since 2018, conceded the race in a video posted to X. "While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," the 67-year-old senator said. "I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state."

stories.title: USA withdraws from U17 World Cup over safety concerns
stories.summary: The USA has withdrawn its national team from the men's FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar over safety concerns. In a letter sent to players the federation said it was cancelling the team's pre-tournament camp and its participation in the event "in light of current circumstances." It cited the US State Department's Level 3 travel advisory for Qatar and related directives for embassy staff and families. "The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority," the letter said. US Soccer said it would notify the players' clubs on Wednesday. It asked players not to comment publicly until FIFA announces the decision. The US State Department updated its advisory for Qatar last month, urging Americans to reconsider travel because of the risk of armed conflict.

stories.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin
stories.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, part of their latest push for a peace deal in Ukraine. The Kremlin talks - expected to take place in the first half of the day - will be the 10th time that Mr Witkoff has met Mr Putin in person, and follow two days of trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi which finished on Wednesday with news of another planned major prisoner exchange but no public breakthrough in wider negotiations. The two envoys are due to meet Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin later today. Kirill Dmitriev, Mr Putin's special envoy, met Mr Kushner and Mr Witkoff off their plane amid wet snow and accompanied them to central Moscow ahead of their talks with Putin. This week's Abu Dhabi talks were the first direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine mediated by the US to try to end the war and, although Russian and Ukrainian negotiators reported some progress, the US side said differences remained on major issues, including territory. Despite public optimism from US President Trump, there has been no sign of major compromises.

stories.title: Six killed in Israeli strike at Gaza hospital
stories.summary: An Israeli strike killed six people and wounded around 20 at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, a civil defence official said. Gaza's civil defence, a rescue agency operating under Hamas authority, said the bodies of those killed and "more than" 20 people wounded in the strike had been recovered from a building at the medical complex. "The death toll from the Israeli strike inside Nasser Medical Complex, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, has risen to six," civil defence spokesperson Mahmoud Bassal said. A spokesperson for Israel's military said they were checking for information on the incident when asked for comment. Israel and Hamas have accused each other of breaching the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by an attack of unprecedented scale carried out by Hamas against Israel on 7 October 2023. On Tuesday, Israeli forces killed seven people, including a 13-year-old boy, in the Gaza Strip, according to local emergency services, while the Israeli military said it had targeted "military operatives".

stories.title: Hamilton urges Israel to allow aid into Gaza
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton says that Israel must allow aid trucks into Gaza, a day after he visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt. Hamilton, a seven-times Formula One world champion, arrived in El Arish on Tuesday, where he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses. "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling. It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less," the Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram. Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide and says its military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas militants. Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go at the border that were regularly held up or faced major delays. He said that at a nearby logistics centre, items had been rejected for "crazy reasons", including sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, and footballs for children.

stories.title: Zelensky thanks Ireland for 'unwavering support'
stories.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has thanked Ireland for its "unwavering support for our people, for Ukraine, for our defence". Speaking alongside Taoiseach Micheál Martin following their bilateral meeting at Government Buildings yesterday, Mr Zelensky said: "Ireland has always shown a full understanding of what's happening in Ukraine, and most importantly, of just how unjust Russia’s aggression is against all of us, against Ukraine, and against normal, peaceful life, peaceful life in Europe." He said he had briefed Mr Martin on the current situation in Ukraine and the difficulty in restoring its infrastructure. "I’m grateful for the willingness to help Ukraine and for the support packages. All of these packages are extremely important," he said. "This war is in Ukraine, and ending this war without Europe's participation would be unjust, and it would be impossible," he said. Mr Martin described the meeting, which comes ahead of the European Political Community meeting in Dublin today, as coming at "such an important time for Ukraine".

stories.title: RTÉ Sport staff vote 'no confidence' in leadership team
stories.summary: It comes after issues regarding the 'Howler' sports podcast, presented by Ger Gilroy. It said that staff have been "consistently" told that the era of "murky practices, secret deals and a general lack of transparency is in the past", but "the events of the last weeks have shown us in fact that nothing has changed". The statement described the "apparent a-la-carte adherence to transparent HR practices" as having "aggrieved Sports staff who face a number of longstanding issues including incorrect grading, career progression and a lack of programme resourcing, including underinvestment in technology". "We believe the values of public service broadcasting have been trumped by commercial interests," members said, adding that "nowhere is the abandonment of public service values more evident than in the lack of women’s voices on the new podcast in its first few weeks". "For clarity, this is not an NUJ motion, but an internal branch motion," the statement said. The broadcaster said that Director-General Kevin Bakhurst is scheduled to meet staff in the sports department next week.

stories.title: Two men who 'terrorised' Clare postmistress jailed
stories.summary: A judge has imposed cumulative prison terms of 13 years on two armed men who "terrorised" a postmistress during a "callous" robbery of a rural Co Clare post office earlier this year. At Ennis Circuit Court, Judge Francis Comerford said the armed, premeditated and violent robbery of Carrigaholt Post Office on 21 January carried out by 39-year-old Michael McMahon, of Plunkett Drive in Kilkishen, and 39-year-old Darren Cassidy, of Lifford Mews, Lifford in Ennis, as callous in its planning and callous in its execution. Judge Comerford said the men had carried out the robbery "out of desperation", but in their desperation had terrorised the "remarkably brave and resilient" postmistress, Maura McKiernan, during the robbery. Judge Comerford said the robbers had chosen the "easy target" of the post office in a rural area of west Clare. In the mid-afternoon on 21 January, McMahon and Cassidy entered the post office dressed in white overalls, black hoods and black gloves. They were each armed with an iron bar and one of the two handed in a bag at the counter to be filled with money.

stories.title: Hospital apology for care deficiencies after baby's death
stories.summary: A hospital has apologised in court to the parents of a baby boy who died 30 days after his birth. The apology, from Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital Drogheda, in Co Louth, was read to the High Court as the parents of Kayden Brogan Mullen settled their action against the Health Service Executive. The letter, from the hospital's Chief Executive Priya Madhu, said that it recognised the loss of baby Kayden had a profound and devastating effect on the couple and it apologised for the deficiencies in care. The action was taken by Kayden's parents, Keira Brogan and Richard Mullen, from Carlanstown, Kells in Co Meath. The court heard that Ms Brogan’s pregnancy was identified as high risk, and she had attended the hospital for scans and reviews. On 18 February 2022, she went to the hospital with reduced foetal movements.

stories.title: Tight security restrictions to disrupt travel in Dublin
stories.summary: Travelling around Dublin is expected to be challenging this morning and this evening as tighter security restrictions come into operation on the first day of the European Political Community meeting. The ninth EPC summit at the Convention Centre Dublin is the largest diplomatic undertaking in Irish history. The public is being advised to avoid moving between the Convention Centre in the north city and Merrion Square in the south city, in particular in the afternoon and evening. Since 8pm last night, the security cordon around the Convention Centre has been increased, resulting in the closure of the Samuel Beckett Bridge until Friday. Merrion Square is also under a larger lockdown since 7am. This will remain in place until midnight, as the political leaders are due to attend a dinner in the National Gallery. Traffic and parking restrictions are continuing around hotels in the north and south city associated with the event until late Friday evening.

stories.title: Europe has a lot to gain by working closely - Taoiseach
stories.summary: The Taoiseach has said that Europe has a lot to gain by working closely together on shared challenges. Micheál Martin will host the ninth meeting of the European Political Community in the Convention Centre Dublin. He will greet the EU and non-EU leaders arriving for the meeting as well as speak at the opening and closing of the summit. Mr Martin paid tribute to the collaboration right across the public service in preparing for the biggest gathering of world leaders the country has ever hosted, plans for which have been under way for more than than a year. More than 2,000 people are working on the event at the Convention Centre, where 47 world leaders will gather. The theme of today's meeting is 'Europe - strong, secure and connected'.

stories.title: Former footballer of the year Conroy announces retirement
stories.summary: Paul Conroy has announced his retirement from inter-county Gaelic football 18 years after making his debut for Galway. Conroy played 151 times for the Tribesmen with his final appearance coming in this year's All-Ireland quarter-final defeat to Dublin. He first played for Galway in 2008, having captained the county to a minor All-Ireland title the year before. His senior career in maroon and white saw him land seven Connacht medals. Conroy was part of Galway squads that reached All-Ireland finals in 2022 and 2024, starting in both matches as the team came up short against Kerry and Armagh. In 2024, the St. James' clubman became just the third Galway footballer to win footballer of the year, following from Ja Fallon (1998) and Declan Meehan (2001). He was awarded his only All-Star in the same year. "Privileged to have fulfilled a childhood dream getting to represent an amazing county for so many years.

stories.title: USA cancel media plans as United close on Pochettino
stories.summary: The United States have cancelled media access scheduled for today as Manchester United prepare to make a move for their head coach Mauricio Pochettino. It's understood plans are afoot at United to recruit the Argentinian should current head coach Michael Carrick, as expected, be dismissed, with the club in the relegation zone on the back of their worst start to a season since 1986. Pochettino is understood to be interested in the Old Trafford post, having also been linked with the vacancy when it has arisen in the past. US Soccer confirmed planned media access with players scheduled for Wednesday had been cancelled in observance of Veterans Day, which removed the possibility of Pochettino's squad being asked to comment on the news of his potential exit. Former Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea boss Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain as US head coach through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago and US Soccer would be due compensation should he agree to move to United. Despite the speculation surrounding Carrick, the Englishman arrived for training as usual at United's Carrington training ground on Wednesday morning.

stories.title: GAA games development chair: No change to teen structure
stories.summary: The chair of the GAA's National Games Development Committee Micheál Martin says that games at teenage level will remain competitive. It emerged on Tuesday that proposals were being prepared to consider changing the nature of underage GAA matches, with the aim of improving the retention of players in the 13 to 17 bracket. Research work by a team of academics is set to highlight how the rate of dropout of players from aged 12 upwards is high, and suggested measures to address this included the possible modification of rules, small-sided games, and offering a less competitive environment. Last month the GAA Games Development department published a 'Cohesion, Clarity and Consistency’ report, led by Martin. This work also targeted long-standing structural and participation challenges across the association and addressed issues with adolescent participation and high rates of player drop-off. In addition, it shone a light on volunteer withdrawal and other challenges facing coaching and development personnel.
